reader.requirement: At --std 85, in a format-1 data description entry the data-name-1 or FILLER (optional in 1985) must come directly after the level-number, a REDEFINES clause must come directly after that name or, when no name is written, directly after the level-number, and every other clause (PICTURE, USAGE, SIGN, OCCURS, SYNC, JUST, BLANK WHEN ZERO, VALUE) is accepted in any order.

edition-consulted.switches: whether a reservation-gated word after the level-number is read as data-name-1 (the edition's reserved-word set); not the clause-order rule itself

reader.edition-search: Read ScreenLeadingClausePosition and its caller in BindEntry (DataBinder.cs:3778): no edition test, it asks the written clause ordinal; grep of DataBinder.ClausePlacement.cs for DialectLevel/ConstructRegistry/Edition.Edition finds only SynchronizedViolation (another rule). The name-first half is the grammar: dataDescriptionEntry is levelNumber dataName? dataDescriptionBody, so a name after a clause falls to unrecognizedDataClause (COBOL1941) at every edition.
reader.witnesses-cover: part: g85_bf09_01 covers the three legal REDEFINES placements and several free clause orders; it does not exercise the refusal half (REDEFINES after another clause, name after a clause, FILLER after REDEFINES)

reader.notes: The name-first half is grammatical (an optional dataName slot only right after levelNumber); the REDEFINES half is ScreenLeadingClausePosition's ordinal test, and the free-order half is dataDescriptionClause*. Diagnostics cite §2023 clauses (13.18.44.3 SR1, 13.16.2) rather than the 1985 rule; the behaviour is the 1985 requirement.
